sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: one retailer's printed return set against whichever of two printed benchmark ranges matches the way the return was measured; the basis is stated in one document and the rule for matching in the other; medium (hard acceptable); measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 1 l172 ROACE 12.7% (Woolworths NZ, average of 2015 to 2019); Doc 1 l179-180 right of use assets for leased property included in capital employed; Doc 11 l152-154 leased assets included gives the unlevered return (Column D), IFRS 16 values serve as the asset value; Doc 11 l159 unlevered overseas range approximately 9 to 11 per cent; Doc 11 l162 the same range at a renter's leverage, approximately 22 to 25 per cent; Doc 11 l277 benchmarks fit only returns with all assets in capital employed; 12.7 - 11 = 1.7.
- Universe: not applicable (one value). The two candidate ranges are the only ranges of overseas grocers' returns on capital in the bundle.
- Necessity: Doc 1 is the only document that prints 12.7% or says how Woolworths NZ's figure was measured (searched "12.7", "ROACE", "right of use", "ROU", "IFRS", "whole of business", "leases most" in all 13; Doc 8 l602 mentions "whole of business" calculations with no values; Doc 5 l136 mentions IFRS16 with no values). Doc 11 is the only document with either range or the matching rule (searched "9 per cent", "11 per cent", "22 per cent", "25 per cent", "unlevered", "levered", "international sample"; Doc 8 l627-628 speaks of benchmarking against international grocery retailers without a figure; Doc 1 l185-188 mentions a sample of overseas grocery retailers for profit margins only, with no figure). Remove Doc 1 and the ROACE and its basis are unreachable; remove Doc 11 and the range is unreachable. Each supplies its own operand of the subtraction.
- Selected-lever checks: Calculate across documents: one subtraction of a Doc 11 figure from a Doc 1 figure. No which-items decoy or rounding lever is claimed.
- Targeted failure modes: Unit or basis, recomputed: 25 - 12.7 = 12.3 below the top of the renter-leverage range (22 - 12.7 = 9.3 below its bottom); the passage that sets it is Doc 1 l179 ("leases most of the land and buildings") beside Doc 11 l162; no measured attempts yet. Considered and not declared: the Commission's own normal return of 5.5% (Doc 1 l174), 12.7 - 5.5 = 7.2, a different benchmark that the wording rules out by naming the consultant's overseas range; the bottom of the range, 12.7 - 9 = 3.7, ruled out by "top"; Foodstuffs NI (13.1, 2.1) and Foodstuffs SI (12.8, 1.8), ruled out by the retailer's name.
- Calculation verification: python, 2026-10-12 (caller): round(12.7 - 11, 1) = 1.7; round(25 - 12.7, 1) = 12.3; round(12.7 - 5.5, 1) = 7.2; round(12.7 - 9, 1) = 3.7. Inputs are percentages; the result is in percentage points; no rounding is needed.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: searched "1.7", "percentage point" in all 13: Doc 11 l150 prints only its example's 12.60 percentage point increase and l280 a 0.30 percentage point WACC effect; no document sets a retailer's ROACE against either range. Bundle overview: Doc 1's line lists the three ROACEs and 5.5%, Doc 11's line lists "9-11% average unlevered ROACE for international grocery retailers" and "22-25% adjusted benchmark for leveraged returns", so both ranges are visible there with their labels; the overview does not say which basis the final report used for Woolworths NZ. Shortest complete route: Doc 1 l172 and l179-180, Doc 11 l152-162, one subtraction.
- Precision/readings: both ranges are stated as "approximately"; the answer uses the printed top, 11, and one decimal place follows the printed 12.7. Doc 11 fn 15 says the Commission "envisages only publishing whole-of-business returns" for Woolworths and l308 pairs "unlevered" with "whole of business", which agrees with the reading. Doc 11 l72 describes a store-level renter measure the Commission intended for Foodstuffs at the conference; it concerns Foodstuffs' stores, not Woolworths NZ, and Doc 1 l178 shows the final report did not use it.
- Completeness: no source gaps; all 13 documents read in full.
- Style/set review: one live question. The sibling wording on Foodstuffs NI (ideas.md, i01b, 2.1 above) shares this answer path: submit at most one. Sketch i02 uses different documents and a different mechanism.
- Warnings answered: see the hand-over.
sections.question: How far, in percentage points, is Woolworths NZ's 2015 to 2019 ROACE in the Commission's final report from the top of the range of overseas grocers' returns that Foodstuffs' profitability consultant treats as comparable with a return measured that way?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 1, the final report's profitability finding): the Commission's estimate of Woolworths NZ's return on average capital employed (ROACE), averaged over five years, is 12.7%.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 1, the same finding, on what changed after the draft report): for Woolworths NZ the report now includes right of use assets, the value of leased property, in capital employed. Woolworths NZ leases most of the land and buildings its stores use, so the question turns on how that leased property was treated, not on who owns it.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 11, section 2.1, the consultant's first option): a return calculated with the leased assets included, their value in the denominator and their depreciation in the numerator, is an unlevered return, the outcome in Column D of the consultant's worked example. A return that leaves rented property out is a levered one. The consultant says a benchmark fits only returns measured with all assets in capital employed unless it is raised to the same leverage.

Step 4. Source input (Doc 11, section 2.1, the consultant's second option): the average unlevered return on capital employed of the international sample of grocery retailers was between approximately 9 per cent and 11 per cent. Restated at the leverage of stores assumed to rent their land and buildings, that range becomes approximately 22 per cent to 25 per cent.

Step 5. Matching (Doc 1 and Doc 11): the 12.7% was measured with the leased stores counted in capital employed, so on the consultant's reasoning it is an unlevered return. The comparable range is the unlevered one, whose top is 11 per cent, not the range restated for renters.

Step 6. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 11): 12.7 − 11 = 1.7

Step 7. Final answer (Doc 1 and Doc 11): Woolworths NZ's ROACE is 1.7 percentage points above the top of the comparable range.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Unit or basis
How a careless solver fails: Misapplies a rule or premise

Why these are traps: Unit or basis: Doc 1 says Woolworths NZ leases most stores, so a careless solver treats its ROACE as a renter's levered return, takes Doc 11's 22 to 25 per cent range and answers 12.3 below. The report counted leased stores in capital employed, so 11 applies: 1.7 above.
